idea: Exclude block/end delimiters and a final return from the existing release inlining cost, retaining the raw 96-instruction cap.
result: Default/release throughput instructions improve 1.6%/1.3%, ordinary application compilation 1.2–1.5%; fixed compiler rebuild instructions increase 1.75%. Laptop ordinary throughput latency improves about 0.7–0.8%, but compiler rebuild median increases about 2.0% and that comparison is inconclusive.
decision: The broad policy increases compiler rebuilding work for a modest ordinary-build latency gain. Do not retain it or spend another whole runtime campaign on this version; pursue targeted code-quality improvements instead. This does not establish that all structural-cost models are bad.
validation: 10 focused and 524 quick checks pass; seeds 801..900 pass in five modes. All 16 default artifacts match; all 16 release artifacts differ. Release runtime was not characterized, so no runtime-benefit claim.
